method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.coverageNote: Differentiates polymyositis within the inflammatory myopathy subgroups using the 2017 probability model. Polymyalgia rheumatica referral criteria were not used.

mcqs.question: Which adult subgroups does the criteria paper name as the most common idiopathic inflammatory myopathies?

options.B: Polymyalgia rheumatica, giant-cell arteritis, and gout
options.E: Anti-synthetase syndrome is the only recognized subgroup

mcqs.explanation: The most common adult subgroups are dermatomyositis, polymyositis, and inclusion-body myositis; juvenile dermatomyositis is the childhood subgroup named.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The most common subgroups in adults are dermatomyositis (DM), polymyositis (PM), and inclusion body myositis

mcqs.question: Which candidate classification structure was kept?

options.A: The probability-score model, because it discriminated better than an item count or a tree
options.D: A single mandatory muscle biopsy with no score

mcqs.correctAnswerText: The probability-score model, because it discriminated better than an item count or a tree
mcqs.explanation: Item-count, probability-score, and tree models were examined. The probability-score model had superior discriminating performance, so the others were set aside.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Due to the observed superior discriminating performance of the probability-score model, the other models were set aside.

mcqs.question: How is the probability of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy calculated when a muscle-biopsy score is included?

options.C: 1 / [1 + exponential(6.49 − score)], which is the formula without biopsy
options.E: The paper does not provide a formula

mcqs.explanation: With muscle biopsy, probability = 1 / [1 + exponential(5.33 − score)]. Without biopsy the constant is 6.49.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Probability of IIM including muscle biopsy = 1 / [ 1 + exponential ( 5.33 - score ) ] or, Probability of IIM without muscle biopsy = 1 / [ 1 + exponential ( 6.49 - score ) ]

mcqs.question: What probability cut-point gave the best sensitivity-specificity balance for the criteria without biopsy?
mcqs.explanation: The best balance between sensitivity and specificity was at a probability of 55–60% for the criteria without muscle biopsy.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The best balance between sensitivity and specificity was found for a probability of 55–60% for the criteria n

mcqs.question: Why were new criteria needed, according to the introduction?

options.A: Well-defined patient groups are a prerequisite for trials, and existing diagnostic schemes varied widely
options.B: Polymyositis had been removed as a diagnosis
options.C: Muscle enzymes are no longer measured
options.D: Inclusion-body myositis is the same disease as polymyalgia rheumatica
options.E: Classification is unnecessary if weakness is present

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Well-defined patient groups are a prerequisite for trials, and existing diagnostic schemes varied widely
mcqs.explanation: The paper says a prerequisite for clinical studies is well-defined patient groups, and a wide variety of diagnostic or classification criteria had been in use.
